name: What hidden problems show up during a whole-house remodel?

mainEntity.name: What unexpected issues are most common once demolition starts in an older Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What unexpected issues are most common once demolition starts in an older Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden problems are common in older Los Angeles homes and are one of the main reasons whole-house remodel budgets change. Once walls and floors are opened, contractors may find outdated electrical wiring, corroded plumbing, termite damage, dry rot, slab or foundation issues, asbestos-containing materials, or past unpermitted modifications that must be corrected. Some of these problems are not visible during the initial walkthrough, so a good budget includes contingency funds. Homes built before modern standards may also need safety upgrades that were not obvious during the planning phase. If asbestos or lead-based materials are suspected, testing should happen before demolition begins so the project can be planned safely. The best protection is a thorough pre-construction inspection, engineering review if needed, and a contract that explains how hidden conditions are priced. Homeowners should expect some surprises in older homes and avoid spending the entire budget before the walls are opened.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden issues include old wiring, undersized plumbing, termite damage, dry rot, foundation cracks, asbestos, lead paint, and unpermitted past work. These problems often appear after demolition and can add time, cost, and inspection requirements.
